summary.headline: JSW Cement Q1 FY27 volume rose 15% YoY to 3.81 Mt, but consolidated operating EBITDA fell 7.5% YoY to INR299 crore on North start-up costs and fuel.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 volumes grew 15% YoY to 3.81 million tons, with cement up 27% to 2.34 Mt; ex-North cement volume grew 8%. Consolidated revenue was INR1,896 crore (+22% YoY, flat QoQ) while operating EBITDA fell 7.5% YoY to INR299 crore (INR784/t), as blended fuel cost rose to INR1.80/Mcal from INR1.49 and North marketing spend was about INR33 crore. Management kept high-teens company-wide volume growth guidance for FY27 but cut GGBS growth expectations to high single digits. North breakeven is targeted at EBITDA level in Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt / Net debt to EBITDA

segments.name: North region (new)
segments.commentary: First full quarter of sales; operating loss about INR40 crore including ~INR33 crore marketing; average utilisation ~55% in Q1 and ~68% in June 2026.

segments.name: Cement
segments.commentary: Volume 2.34 Mt (+27% YoY); trade mix stable at 51%; clinker-to-cement factor rose to 55% with North launch; lead distance stable.

segments.name: GGBS
segments.commentary: Volume growth only 2.6% YoY; management cited RMC closures in West, aggregate shortages in South and weak OPC/slag mix economics; South is about 60% of GGBS volume versus 40% West.

segments.name: RMC
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR180 crore; 15 plants operating, 35 more planned; North FY27 revenue target INR1,000 crore including captive group projects.

guidance_outlook: Company-wide volume growth guided at high teens for FY27 including North; management declined to reconcile this with ex-North arithmetic on the call.
GGBS growth revised to high single digits for FY27 (earlier mid-teens); Q2 expected better than Q1, with July signs visible; over 29 large infra approvals received in Q1.
North: EBITDA breakeven targeted in Q2 FY27 and positive by around September; utilisation expected to reach 60%+ by year end.
Clinker costs expected to fall from Q3 as OLBC, AFR, WHRS and lignite/domestic coal ramp; Q2 fuel cost seen similar to Q1.
Capex guided at ~INR2,300 crore for FY27 and ~INR2,000 crore for FY28; long-term target 43.5 Mt, then a further ~25 Mt; net debt/EBITDA internal ceiling below 3.0x.

North marketing spend guided at ~INR130 crore for FY27 (includes technical spend); North capital subsidy of ~INR50 crore/year for first three years expected once eligibility certificate is received (~2 months), recognition tied to capitalisation.
Nagaur 1 Mt grinding expansion due end Q2 FY27; Nagaur 2.5 Mt line due FY28; Fujairah groundbreaking done, operational in ~12 months; Dolvi expansion ~15 months from start.
Vijayanagar Phase 1 pushed beyond CY28 to protect overall utilisation.
capex_capacity: Nagaur integrated unit: WHRS, OLBC and AFR co-processing being installed, expected to commission in the next few weeks.
Nagaur 1 Mt additional grinding on track for end Q2 FY27; capacity 2.5 Mt operating, rising to 3.5 Mt by late Sep/early Oct 2026.
Nagaur project total capex ~INR3,500 crore, of which ~INR2,400–2,500 crore spent to date.
Added 56 MW wind capacity at Dolvi and Vijayanagar in Q1; RE share reached 30%. Management said 60%+ RE share targeted from Q3 FY27, with delays linked to land.
Clinker utilisation 61% including Nagaur (Nandyal, Shiva, Nagaur); 87% excluding Nagaur. Overall cement utilisation 61% in Q1.
Punjab plant: ~INR50–60 crore spent, mainly land; awaiting environmental clearance before work begins; included in capex plan.
demand_pricing: Management estimated cement demand growth of ~6% YoY in South, West and East and ~11% in North in Q1 FY27; central capex up 24% YoY with 28% of FY27 budget used in Q1.
Demand in April and early May hit by labour migration and state elections; June showed strong rebound.
Cement price gap narrowing in A-category band and discount structures reducing, per management; GGBS dispersion attributed to geographic mix, not pricing change.
Infra pipeline cited: Mumbai bullet train, Western Coastal Road, Pune Ring Road, Amaravati, NPCIL Karnataka, Chennai/Kerala roads, residential redevelopment in Mumbai.
Management said South is subdued; North-South profitability gap estimated at INR600–700 per ton.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR33 crore North marketing spend and is the ~INR40 crore North operating loss in line with plan; what full-year North profitability is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Marketing covered a new campaign and ground activations (Khel Mahotsav, cricket in Rajasthan, Dangal in Haryana); it was in the BP and tracking to plan. North should turn profitable, with utilisation at 55% in Q1 and 60%+ by year end; clinker cost relief expected from Q2 as OLBC, AFR and WHRS commission and fuel shifts to domestic coal and lignite.

qa_highlights.question: Why was GGBS growth slow and what growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 hit by West RMC closures, South aggregate shortages and weak OPC/slag economics. Q2 expected better than Q1 with July signs visible; full-year GGBS growth guided to high single digits, with 29+ large infra approvals in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Reconciling company-wide high-teens volume growth with ex-North growth of 8% and GGBS high single digits.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated high-teens company-wide growth including North and GGBS, declined to reconcile it with the analyst's ex-North arithmetic, and said it would take the point offline.

qa_highlights.question: Profitability gap between North and South plants and capex/leverage plans.
qa_highlights.answer: Break-even expected in September; the North-South gap estimated at INR600-700 per ton, with South described as subdued. FY27 capex about INR2,300 crore and FY28 about INR2,000 crore; long-term 43.5 Mt target needs about INR7,500-7,600 crore; net debt/EBITDA internal ceiling below 3.0x.

qa_highlights.question: Timing and amount of the North capital subsidy booking and how it flows through the P&L.
qa_highlights.answer: Not booked yet; eligibility certificate expected in about two months. Recognition tied to capitalisation of WHRS, OLBC and AFR, so the first INR50 crore a year (for three years) will be clearer next quarter. Accounting treatment for the subsidy to be confirmed with auditors.

qa_highlights.question: Fuel cost outlook and RMC plans and economics.
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 fuel cost seen similar to Q1 with domestic coal already being bought; cost decline expected from Q3. RMC: 15 plants, 35 more planned; Q1 RMC revenue about INR180 crore; North FY27 RMC revenue target INR1,000 crore including group captive projects; margins hard to call in the first year.

risks_watch: Whether company-wide high-teens volume growth is achievable given ex-North growth of 8% in Q1 and the unreconciled arithmetic management declined to explain on the call.
GGBS recovery: Q2 must improve on Q1 as promised, with RMC closures in the West, aggregate shortages in the South and the OPC/slag mix still weighing.

North ramp: EBITDA break-even targeted in Q2 FY27 and utilisation of 60%+ by year end depend on Nagaur WHRS, OLBC and AFR commissioning within weeks; marketing spend guided at ~INR130 crore for FY27 and rising as new territories open.
Fuel cost: blended fuel rose to INR1.80/Mcal from INR1.49; Q2 seen flat and relief expected only from Q3, which keeps EBITDA margin under pressure.

Capex and projects: FY27 capex of ~INR2,300 crore and Vijayanagar Phase 1 pushed beyond CY28; Punjab awaiting environmental clearance; Central and Northeast expansion sequencing undecided, with a decision expected in a couple of months.
Accounting and other income items to monitor: North capital subsidy recognition method not yet confirmed; ~INR55 crore one-off from JSW One deconsolidation in other income.
key_quotes: FY27 has started off on a strong note for the company despite the ongoing uncertainty around the West Asia crisis and the impact of state elections held early in the quarter.

Despite improvement in realizations, EBITDA declined mainly due to cost pressures in fuel and packing, plus the substantial marketing investment of about INR33 crores made in North region during quarter one.
So, all that has been planned for quarter two, and we expect the benefits to start to kick in thereafter.
Now, guidance for quarter two FY27, despite Q2 being a monsoon season, we are expecting it to be better than Q1, and signs are visible already in the month of July.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand, the North ramp and cost reduction from Q3, but cautious and at times evasive on FY27 volume arithmetic, the timing of the North subsidy and the Central/Northeast expansion sequence, deferring several of these to later quarters or offline discussion.
